issue.title: test_cross_navigation_and_escape_surface_disabled_workspaces fails under the parallel lane: Workspaces filter is alpha instead of highlighted beta
issue.description:
`tests/ace/tui/modals/test_project_inventory_subtabs.py::test_cross_navigation_and_escape_surface_disabled_workspaces` failed once under the parallel scoped/`just check` lane and passed on a serial rerun of the same tree.

OBSERVED on 2026-08-18 while implementing the Current Project glossary term (sase.yml + generated instruction files only; no ACE/TUI, Projects-tab, or current-project code touched). `just check` in workspace sase_13 escalated to a 33832-item parallel run (`pytest -n 10 --dist=worksteal`): `2 failed, 33830 passed, 13 skipped, 72 warnings in 538.48s`. This node ran on gw0.

EXACT FAILURE (tests/ace/tui/modals/test_project_inventory_subtabs.py:294):
    pane.query_one("#projects-list", OptionList).highlighted = 1
    await pilot.press("w")
    workspace_pane = pane.query_one(WorkspaceInventoryPane)
    assert pane._active_subtab == "workspaces"
    assert workspace_pane.project_filter == "beta"
    E           AssertionError: assert 'alpha' == 'beta'

Index 0 is the enabled fixture project `alpha`; index 1 is the disabled fixture project `beta`. Pressing `w` is supposed to carry the highlighted project into the Workspaces sub-tab filter. The assertion one line above (`_active_subtab == "workspaces"`) passed, so the tab switch happened and only the filter identity was wrong.

NOT REPRODUCED serially: rerunning this node together with `tests/test_ace_testing.py::test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet` on the identical tree with `-n 0` passed in 2.13s (0.56s for this node). Parallel-lane only.

HYPOTHESIS, not a measured root cause: first-open current-project seed of the Repos/Workspaces inventory filters can win a race against the highlighted-row filter. `alpha` is both the default/first fixture project and a plausible seed value. Confirm before designing a fix.

SCOPE: determine whether `w` from a highlighted Projects-tab row must beat the first-open seed, then make that order deterministic. Prefer a mechanism fix over baselining; if it must be baselined first, the `tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt` entry needs this bead named as owner.

This is another node in the retired `sase-ct` "ACE TUI test fails under the full parallel run, passes in isolation" class, filed node-specific per that umbrella's close policy.

---

## Flake report

- **Test:** `tests/ace/tui/modals/test_project_inventory_subtabs.py::test_cross_navigation_and_escape_surface_disabled_workspaces`
- **Repro:** `just check`

Failed once under `just check`'s parallel scoped lane on 2026-08-18 (2 failed / 33830 passed / 13 skipped in 538.48s, gw0); `workspace_pane.project_filter` was `alpha` instead of highlighted `beta` after `w`. Serial rerun on the identical tree passed in 0.56s. Parallel-only. Not previously recorded: `sase bead search` over the node ID, `project_inventory_subtabs`, `project_filter`, and `WorkspaceInventoryPane` found no prior task.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-ct — the retired umbrella for 'ACE TUI test fails under the full parallel run, passes in isolation'. DO NOT +1 or reopen it; its close reason mandates exactly this route (a narrow node-specific bead plus a RELATED note). This bead exists because of that policy.

RELATED: sase-oz — the other node that failed in the same just check run (test_ace_page_fast_startup_is_structurally_quiet, leftover sase-artifacts-project-choices task). Same run, same lane, different mechanism: sase-oz is AcePage teardown, this one is Projects-tab Workspaces filter identity after w. Listed as a run sibling, not a duplicate.

RELATED: sase-qd — in-progress epic 'Show and set the current project from the Admin Center Projects tab'. Topical overlap only: this flake is on the Projects-tab Workspaces sub-tab, but the suspected race is first-open current-project seed (closed epic sase-pw) vs highlighted-row filter, not the set-current keypress sase-qd landed. Do not treat this as a DISCOVERED ISSUE on sase-qd unless a later repro ties it to that epic's write path.

Root-caused and fixed during the sase-qd epic landing; the hypothesis in this report (first-open seed racing the highlighted row) was close but not the mechanism. Real cause: sase-qd.2 (commit ec048b168) replaced the seed-only current-project worker with a display resolve whose completion handler called ProjectsPane._refresh_options() with no preferred project. _refresh_options prefers _session_state.projects.identity (the bookmark) over the live OptionList.highlighted, and OptionHighlighted reaches the pane only after bubbling out of the option list's own message queue -- so a resolve posted straight to the pane can overtake it and repaint from the stale bookmark, snapping the highlight back to index 0 (alpha). This is a real user-facing regression, not only a test artifact: the same window exists on mount, on R, and after a successful c set. Fix: _apply_current_project_display now repaints through _repaint_for_current_project(), which passes preferred_project=self._selected_project_name(), mirroring what the inventory worker's completion handler already did. Verified: the node failed 4/12 serial runs before the fix and passed 15/15 after; added tests/ace/tui/test_projects_pane_current_project_seed.py::test_resolve_repaint_keeps_a_row_the_bookmark_has_not_caught_up_to, which fails on the pre-fix tree (highlighted 0 != 1) and passes after; also stubbed resolve_current_project in this module's _patch_inventory_data so the suite no longer reads the developer's real MRU. No baseline entry was needed.

The 2026-08-19T01:12:58Z close was made by sase-qd.land, which root-caused the node (ec048b168's resolve-completion repaint overtaking OptionHighlighted and repainting from the stale bookmark) but has not committed that fix.   20260819T004329Z  head a317a2e359e8  ws sase_12  full parallel lane

IMPACT, which is new: this node has now crossed the flake-baseline gate's bar. `just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake`, the last step of `just check-full`, names it as one of three reproducible flakes exceeding tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt, so it is red for every agent landing on master, not just for the unlucky run. I am adding a baseline entry naming this bead per that file's header, with a comment pointing at sase-qd's pending fix; whoever commits that fix should replace the entry with a `# fixed-at:` line rather than merely deleting it, so the pre-fix evidence retires correctly.
